body.text: Every listing carries the date someone from the guide last stood in the doorway, and the source of what it says. Nothing is copied from a directory or inferred from a category.
If the bakery has not confirmed its winter Mondays, the listing shows no hours rather than a guess, and asks you to call ahead. A cancelled event stays visible so nobody drives out for it.

payload.summary: A resident-written guide to Pine Hollow, Colorado: places worth the drive, events worth the evening, and the small facts that make a visit go well.
payload.title: Home

body.text: The front room is new titles and maps; the back room is used paperbacks priced by the inch. The owner runs the reading nights at the library and will special-order anything the distributor carries within a week.

payload.summary: New and used books in two small rooms, with a strong shelf of regional history and a resident cat who ignores everyone.
payload.title: Aspen Street Books

body.text: At 6:28 the light is still behind Saddle Ridge and the window is already open. The first order is a black coffee for a man who has ordered a black coffee every morning for eleven years. The second is a cortado for someone who moved here in June and is trying hard to become a regular.

By seven the roaster is loud enough to end conversation, which is the point: the bench outside becomes the place where the town's weather predictions are settled. By nine the rush is over and the owner starts bagging beans for the Mercantile shelf.
If you go

items: Ask what is roasting; it changes weekly
The creek path starts behind the building

payload.summary: Six-thirty on a Tuesday: the roaster is running, the dog walkers are arguing about snow, and the bench is already full.
payload.title: A morning at Creekside Coffee Roasters

14e92b57-1809-44ae-a0e1-c62b056412b5.title: A morning at Creekside Coffee Roasters

body.text: The depot lost its trains in 1958 and gained its artists in 1998. Members staff the desk, so the person selling you a print may well have made it. Openings are the best-attended events in town after the harvest market.
Winter hours are shorter and the gallery closes entirely during changeovers; check the events list before driving out.

payload.summary: Cooperative gallery in the former rail depot: paintings, weaving and photography by valley artists, with a new show every season.
payload.title: Old Depot Gallery

payload.summary: Search the shelves of the public library, renew a loan and book the meeting room with the terrible acoustics.
payload.title: Library catalogue and room bookings

payload.areaDescription: Pull-off on County Road 9, four miles east of town

body.text: The overlook is a quarter mile from the pull-off on County Road 9 and is one of the few viewpoints in the valley that works for wheelchairs and strollers. The railing is new; the drop beyond it is not something to test.
Star parties use the overlook lot because it faces away from town lights. Bring a red flashlight if you join one.

payload.summary: Short paved walk to a railed overlook above a 60-foot waterfall. Loud in June, a ribbon by September, frozen and beautiful in January.
payload.title: Timber Falls Overlook

payload.areaDescription: Trailhead lot 1.5 miles north of town on Miner's Road

body.text: Park at the gravel lot at the end of Miner's Road. The loop runs counter-clockwise by convention so that the steep section is a climb rather than a descent. Expect mud through mid-June and ice on the north side from November.
Before you go

items: Dogs on leash April–July for ground-nesting birds
Cell coverage ends past the second switchback

payload.summary: Four-mile loop with 900 feet of gain, wildflowers in June and the best sunrise bench in the county.
payload.title: Larkspur Loop Trailhead

body.text: The bakery shares a wall with the old assay office and keeps the original tin ceiling. Loaves come out at 7:30; the pie case fills by 9. If you are heading up-valley, the provisions shelf covers the basics: eggs, milk, coffee, batteries and the local honey.
Hours are unverified for the winter season. The owner said they may close Mondays after the first snow; call before making a special trip.

payload.summary: Sourdough, mountain pies and a small grocery shelf for the cabins up the valley. Sells out by noon on Saturdays.
payload.title: Hollow Bakery & Provisions

body.text: Doors open at 6:30. Readings start at 7 and run about an hour, followed by a book table run by Aspen Street Books.

payload.summary: Four valley writers read new work in the library's reading room. Cider, cookies and the wood stove.
payload.title: Autumn Reading Night

body.text: The hall holds 120 seated and has a kitchen, a stage and terrible acoustics that nobody has fixed in forty years. The town council meets here the first Tuesday of the month, and the meeting is open.

items: Accessible entrance on the park side

sections.heading: About the guide
sections.subheading: Who writes it, how listings are verified, and what this demonstration is and is not.

body.text: Pine Hollow is a fictional mountain town, and this guide is a demonstration of a community-guide website. Every place, event, person and phone number on these pages was invented for the demonstration; none of it describes a real business in Colorado or anywhere else.
How a real guide would work

Listings carry a verification date and a source. When a detail is unknown, the page says so rather than guessing: hours are never inferred from a category, and a cancelled event stays visible so nobody drives out for it.

items: Places are checked in person or with the owner
Events come from organizers and are marked cancelled rather than removed
Articles are short, signed and dated

body.text: Corrections and suggestions go through the contact page. Messages are stored with a receipt reference and answered by the editors within a week.

answer.text: Late June to early October for the trails and the pond; the **Harvest Market** in October is the busiest weekend of the year. Winter visits are quiet, and several places keep shorter hours, which the listings show per day.

items.question: When is the best time to visit?

answer.text: In town, yes. It fades past the Mill Pond dam and is gone at Timber Falls, so download directions before you leave the Mercantile.

items.question: Is there mobile coverage in the valley?

answer.text: On a leash at Larkspur Loop and Mill Pond Park. Timber Falls Overlook asks visitors to leave dogs in town because of the drop-offs near the viewpoint.

body.text: The library is a two-room stone building beside the school. Cards are free to anyone in the county. The reading room has a wood stove and is the unofficial warming hut on ski days.

payload.summary: Small library with big windows, a free seed exchange, public computers and the warmest reading room in town.
payload.title: Pine Hollow Public Library

body.text: Every autumn the elk come down from the high country and spend a few weeks in the meadows below Timber Falls. The bugling starts at dusk and carries across the valley; the Ridge House porch is a fine place to hear it with a drink in hand.
Where

items: County Road 9 pull-offs between mile markers 2 and 5
The Mill Pond boathouse at dawn
The Larkspur Loop lower meadow, from the trail only

body.text: How

Stay in or beside your car on the county road. Bulls in the rut are unpredictable and faster than you. Binoculars are better than closeness, and the guide has heard every excuse for the person who wanted the photo.

payload.summary: The herd moves through the lower meadows from late September. Here is where to look, and how not to be the person who gets too close.
payload.title: Where to watch the elk this fall

body.text: Thirty-one volunteers pulled eleven bags of debris and one shopping cart from the pond. Thank you; the boathouse coffee was on the town.

payload.summary: Annual shoreline cleanup before the pond freezes. Waders provided for the brave.
payload.title: Mill Pond Cleanup

body.text: The Larkspur Loop trailhead sits on a strip of county land that nobody wanted until everybody did. In 2004 the trails association agreed to plow it, the county agreed to grade it, and the Mercantile agreed to sell the maps. Twenty years later the arrangement still holds, mostly because nobody has written it down.
Why it matters

Trailheads close when they become a problem for one landowner. Spreading the work across three parties means no single bad winter ends access. It also means the volunteer trail days are not optional: the water bars on the upper switchbacks are the association's half of the bargain.
How to help

items: Join a trail day (see the events list)
Buy the map at the Mercantile; proceeds fund tools
Park inside the lot, not along Miner's Road

body.text: The association's [trail day sign-up form](document:774d4097-6145-4a25-963f-7b63ed077a81) can be printed and left at the Mercantile.

payload.summary: Nobody owns the Larkspur Loop lot, which is exactly why it stays plowed. A short history of the valley's volunteer trail deal.
payload.title: How Pine Hollow keeps its trailheads open

payload.attribution: Town of Pine Hollow parks notice (fictional)

body.text: The pond was dug for the sawmill in the 1890s and has been the town's swimming hole for a century. The path is flat and stroller-friendly. The town posts an ice-safety sign at the boathouse in winter; if the sign is not out, stay off the ice.

items: Picnic tables first come, first served

payload.summary: Town park around the old mill pond: a half-mile path, picnic tables, a swimming beach in July and skating when the ice is posted safe.
payload.title: Mill Pond Park

body.text: The county astronomy club sets up four telescopes at the overlook. Arrive before dark to park without headlights on the group, and bring a red flashlight. The event runs past midnight, so the listed end time is on the following calendar day.

payload.summary: Telescopes on the overlook lot from dusk until well past midnight. Dress for winter even in September.
payload.title: Star Party at Timber Falls

body.text: Ask for Dee. The shop is a converted garage, so the door is usually open and the radio is usually on. Rentals are old but tuned, and the price includes a helmet and a map of the pond loop.

payload.summary: One-mechanic shop behind the fire station. Same-day flats, tune-ups by appointment, loaner bikes for visitors.
payload.title: Foothill Bike Repair

payload.admission: Free; sign up at the trails association site

body.text: Meet at the trailhead lot. Work is on the upper switchbacks, so expect a mile of walking before the first shovel. Wear boots. Under-16s need an adult along.

payload.summary: Help rebuild the water bars on the steep section before the snow. Tools, gloves and lunch provided.
payload.title: Larkspur Loop Volunteer Trail Day

body.text: The gallery cooperative cancelled the opening after the October storm damaged the depot roof. The show itself is postponed to spring; this listing stays visible so nobody drives out for it.

payload.summary: Opening reception for the winter show. Cancelled this year while the depot roof is repaired.
payload.title: Depot Gallery Opening: Winter Light

body.text: Creekside opens before the sun clears the ridge, which is why half the town's dog walkers end up on its bench by seven. The roaster runs Tuesday and Friday mornings; if the door is propped open, you will smell it from the footbridge.
Order at the window in summer or inside from October on. Cards and cash are both fine. The creek path behind the building connects to Mill Pond Park in about ten minutes on foot.
Good to know

items: Beans sold by the half pound

nextAction.label: Plan a walk to Mill Pond Park

payload.summary: Small-batch roaster on the creek path with a walk-up window, early hours and the town's most reliable weather chatter.
payload.title: Creekside Coffee Roasters

body.text: The association posts trail conditions on Fridays through the season and cancels a trail day on its own site first. Membership is by donation; the sign-up form is on the trailheads article.

payload.summary: Trail conditions, the volunteer day calendar and the map the Mercantile sells, from the people who keep the Larkspur Loop open.
payload.title: Pine Hollow Trails Association

body.text: The Ridge House has been the town's living room since the mine closed. The porch faces west, so evenings are the draw: bring a layer, because the temperature drops fast once the sun goes behind Saddle Ridge.
Kitchen hours are shorter than bar hours. Reservations are only taken for groups of eight or more; everyone else waits on the porch with a drink.
Good to know

items: Parking is on Aspen Street, not on the lane

payload.summary: Timber-frame tavern with a long porch, a short menu that changes weekly and live music most Saturdays.
payload.title: The Ridge House Tavern

body.text: If Pine Hollow has a town square, it is the Mercantile's front step. The store stocks what the valley actually needs: stove parts, snow shovels in October, seed potatoes in April, and a wall of wool. Fishing and hunting licenses are sold at the back counter.

payload.summary: Hardware, wool socks, fishing licenses and the only key-cutting machine for thirty miles. Open since 1921.
payload.title: Hollow Mercantile

body.text: Forty vendors line Aspen Street from the Mercantile to the bookshop. Come early for eggs and late for deals on squash. The street reopens to cars at 5 p.m.

payload.summary: Aspen Street closes to cars for the valley's growers, bakers and makers. Music from noon, cider all day.
payload.title: Harvest Market on Aspen Street
